chief_complaint: left lower quadrant pain and fever
hpi_details: 70F presents with 3 days of constant left lower quadrant abdominal pain, fever, and constipation.

investigation_events.title: Urgent diverticulitis results
investigation_events.availability_message: The urgent diverticulitis results are now available.

results.test: CT abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast
results.value: Sigmoid diverticulosis with focal colonic wall thickening and pericolic fat stranding; no abscess, free air, or obstruction

core_concepts: LLQ pain, fever, and leukocytosis are classic.
common_misconceptions: Ordering a colonoscopy in the acute phase (contraindicated due to perforation risk).
management_principles: CT scan with IV contrast to diagnose and stage; antibiotics and clear liquids for uncomplicated cases.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

source_refs.title: SAGES & ACS Evidence-Based Surgical Practice Guidelines

reference_soap.plan: CT abdomen/pelvis with contrast to confirm uncomplicated disease and exclude abscess or perforation. Use supportive care with oral hydration, analgesia, and dietary advancement as tolerated; reserve antibiotics for complicated disease, systemic illness, immunocompromise, or other higher-risk presentations. Provide prompt return precautions for worsening pain, fever, vomiting, or inability to tolerate oral intake.

learning_objectives: Identify acute diverticulitis and avoid acute colonoscopy.

teaching.one_liner: Left lower quadrant pain, fever, and changes in bowel habits indicative of acute diverticulitis.

must_ask.say: Is the pain mainly in your lower left side, and is it constant?
Have you noticed any changes in your bowel movements, such as constipation or diarrhea?
Have you had a fever or chills?
Have you noticed any blood in your stool?
Have you had similar episodes of belly pain before, or a known history of diverticulosis?

history.answer: My lower belly on the left side has been hurting for the past three days, and I've also had a fever.
It started gradually about three days ago, and the pain has been steady and slowly getting worse since then.
The pain is right in my left lower belly, and it hasn't shifted or moved anywhere else.
No, it doesn't shoot into my back, down to my groin, or up to my shoulders.
It feels like a deep, constant ache and cramp rather than sharp stabbing or sudden waves.
I would rate it about a 6 out of 10 right now, but it was milder when it first began.
Walking around or pressing on the area makes it hurt worse, and resting quietly is the only thing that slightly helps.
No, I have never had an episode of belly pain like this before.
I have felt a little nauseous, but I haven't thrown up anything.
I haven't had a bowel movement in three days, which is unusual because I am normally very regular.
No, I haven't seen any red blood, dark black stools, or mucus.
Yes, I took my temperature at home yesterday and it was around 38 degrees, with mild chills.
No, my eyes and skin look normal, and my urine hasn't turned dark brown or tea-colored.
No burning or pain when I pee, no blood in my urine, and I'm not going to the bathroom more often than usual.
No, I haven't felt faint or lightheaded when standing up.
No, I haven't had any unusual vaginal discharge or spotting at all.
No chest pain, heart flutter, or trouble breathing at all.
history.topic: Chest pain or shortness of breath

history.answer: I have just been eating light home-cooked meals, nothing especially greasy, and no raw food.
I took one acetaminophen pill yesterday, but it didn't relieve the pain, and I haven't taken aspirin or ibuprofen.
No, my doctor has never told me I have an irregular heartbeat or clogged blood vessels.
I'm worried I might have some sort of bowel infection that is causing the inflammation.
A close friend of mine was recently diagnosed with colon cancer, so I'm terrified that this might be a tumor.
I'm hoping to get an accurate diagnosis and find out if I need antibiotics or hospitalization to make it go away.
I have had high blood pressure for about ten years, but no other chronic illnesses like diabetes.
I had my appendix taken out when I was twenty, but I've never had any other surgeries or hospital stays.
I take lisinopril 10 milligrams once a day every morning for my blood pressure.
No, I have no known allergies to any medications, foods, or materials.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used any tobacco products.
I don't drink alcohol, not even socially.
I am a retired teacher and live in an apartment with my husband.
My father had hypertension, but there is no family history of colon cancer, inflammatory bowel disease, or early heart disease.
I went through menopause naturally over twenty years ago, around age 50.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 130/80 mmHg, heart rate 88 beats per minute, respiratory rate 16 breaths per minute, oxygen saturation 98% on room air, and temperature 38.0°C.
Alert, lying still in mild discomfort due to abdominal pain, without toxic appearance.
Conjunctivae are pink without pallor, and sclerae are non-icteric.
Abdomen is flat with an old well-healed appendectomy scar in the right lower quadrant, with no distension or visible pulsations.
Hypoactive bowel sounds are present in all four quadrants with no abdominal bruits.
Tenderness and mild voluntary guarding localized to the left lower quadrant without palpable masses.
No rebound tenderness or involuntary rigidity in any quadrant.
Negative Murphy's sign with no tenderness in the right upper quadrant.
No tenderness at McBurney's point, and both psoas and obturator signs are negative.
No costovertebral angle tenderness on either side.
Normal sphincter tone, no palpable mass or focal tenderness, and no gross blood on the examining glove.
